title: 2D Shape Recognition Worksheets for Kindergarten
intro: Teach shape names through sides and corners rather than orientation.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Have the student trace the shape and describe its features. Rotate an example and ask whether its name changes.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

The square on this worksheet rests on a corner. It has four equal straight sides and four square corners. Its mathematical name is still square. The word “diamond” may describe its appearance in everyday conversation, but square is the name used for this picture in the answer key.

Trace all the way around the picture before naming it. Turning the page can help a child recognize the square, then check that the same edges are present when the page turns back.

Ask your student

What stays the same when we turn this shape?

If your student needs help

If writing is a barrier, accept a spoken name and record it for the student.
